text: Right. I've been thinking about the ending all afternoon and I'm not budging. The whole film is about her refusing to be the person everyone needs her to be, and the last scene is the only place she actually does it. The cut to the empty platform is the point, not a cop-out. Dan, you said it felt like they ran out of money, which is an insult to the editor. I also found this interview with the director where he more or less says the same thing, so I'm not making it up: https://www.example.com/director-interview
